questions.text: Does it have 50 or more employees?
questions.help: Count everyone on the establishment's file with the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. Emiratisation targets for skilled jobs apply from 50 employees.

questions.text: Does it have 20 to 49 employees and work in one of the 14 sectors named for Emiratisation?
questions.help: The sectors are: information and communications; financial and insurance activities; real estate; professional, scientific and technical activities; administrative and support services; education; healthcare and social work; arts and entertainment; mining and quarrying; manufacturing; construction; wholesale and retail trade; transportation and warehousing; hospitality.

questions.text: Do any of its staff work outdoors, under direct sunlight or in open places?
questions.help: For example on construction sites, roads, farms or deliveries on foot. The midday break applies to this work in summer.

questions.text: Does it hold an establishment card to sponsor residence visas?
questions.help: The establishment card (immigration file) is issued by the Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs and Port Security, or by the residency directorate in Dubai. A business needs it to sponsor staff or partners.

questions.text: Is it a dealer in precious metals or precious stones?
questions.help: Gold, jewellery, diamonds and similar. These dealers file a separate report for large cash and company transactions.

questions.text: Is it a real estate broker or agent?
questions.help: Brokers and agents file a separate report for freehold sales paid in cash or with virtual assets.

questions.text: Does it handle personal data, for example of employees, customers or suppliers?
questions.help: The DIFC treats an entity that hires employees or serves customers as processing personal data. Such entities register with the data protection commissioner of their financial centre.

questions.text: Is it a small private company?
questions.help: The DIFC handbook describes a small private company as one with 20 or fewer shareholders, or an annual turnover of USD 5 million or less. Small companies have longer to file accounts.
Each free zone sets its own rules for filing audited accounts.

questions.text: Has it been told by its Abu Dhabi sector regulator to run an approved occupational safety and health management system?
questions.help: Under the Abu Dhabi Occupational Safety and Health System Framework (ADOSH-SF, formerly OSHAD-SF), nominated medium and high risk entities have an approved system and report to their sector regulatory authority.

questions.text: Do you hold an Emirates ID?
questions.help: Every UAE citizen and resident must hold a valid Emirates ID card.

questions.text: Do you live in the UAE on a residence visa?
questions.help: For example a visa sponsored by your employer or a family member, or a Golden or Green residence.

compliances.name: Emiratisation target (50 or more employees)
compliances.head: Emiratisation
compliances.authority: Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation
compliances.brief: Private sector establishments with 50 or more employees must raise the share of UAE nationals in their skilled jobs by 2 per cent every year, to reach an overall increase of 10 per cent by 2026. A company that falls short pays a monthly amount for each national it did not employ.
compliances.why: It has 50 or more employees and is registered with MoHRE.
compliances.appliesInWords: Private sector establishments with 50 or more employees.

due.text: Each year: 2 per cent more UAE nationals in skilled jobs

compliances.dueText: Raise Emiratisation rates by 2 per cent annually for skilled jobs, to achieve an overall rate of increase of 10 per cent by 2026.
compliances.penalty: AED 6,000 a month (2023 level) for every UAE national not employed against the target; the amount increases by AED 1,000 each year until 2026.
compliances.evidence: raise Emiratisation rates to 2 per cent annually for skilled jobs in private sector establishments with 50 or more employees ... Since 2023, non-compliant companies have been required to pay an amount of AED 6,000 monthly ... These contributions increase by AED 1,000 annually until 2026.
compliances.note: The u.ae page gives the yearly rate only. The half-year split (1 per cent by 30 June and 1 per cent by 31 December) appears in search-result snippets of mohre.gov.ae, but that site returned HTTP 503 to every request on 2026-11-11 and was not opened. No rule for 2027 onward was found.

compliances.name: Emiratisation target (20 to 49 employees in 14 sectors)
compliances.head: Emiratisation
compliances.authority: Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation
compliances.brief: Since 2024, private companies with 20 to 49 workers in 14 named sectors must hire UAE nationals: at least one by the end of 2024 and one more by the end of 2025. A company that did not pays a yearly amount.
compliances.why: It has 20 to 49 employees and works in one of the named sectors.
compliances.appliesInWords: Private sector companies with a workforce of 20 to 49 workers in the 14 named sectors.

due.text: One UAE national by end of 2024 and one more by end of 2025

compliances.dueText: Hire at least one UAE citizen by end of 2024, and one more Emirati by end of 2025.
compliances.penalty: AED 96,000 charged in January 2025 for not hiring one Emirati in 2024; AED 108,000 in January 2026 for not hiring two Emiratis in 2025.
compliances.evidence: hire at least one UAE citizen by end of 2024 ... Additionally, they are required to hire one more Emirati by end of 2025 ... AED 108,000 in January 2026 for failing to hire two Emiratis in 2025.
compliances.note: The page states targets only up to the end of 2025. Whether a further hire or payment applies for 2026 and later was not found on an official page (mohre.gov.ae returned HTTP 503).

compliances.name: Midday break for outdoor work
compliances.head: Workplace safety
compliances.authority: Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation
compliances.brief: Every summer, work under direct sunlight and in open places is not allowed in the middle of the day. Some jobs are exempt for technical reasons.
compliances.why: Its staff work outdoors.
compliances.appliesInWords: Employers whose workers work under direct sunlight or in open places.
compliances.dueText: No work under direct sunlight and in open places between 12.30 pm and 3 pm, from 15 June to 15 September of every year.
compliances.evidence: All work performed under direct sunlight and in open places shall not be allowed between the peak hours of 12.30 pm and 3 pm, from 15 June to 15 September of every year.
compliances.note: The date shown is the first day of the ban; it runs until 15 September. The u.ae page states no fine. A fine per worker is quoted in MoHRE announcements, but mohre.gov.ae could not be opened (HTTP 503), so it is not given here.

compliances.name: Report a workplace injury or death
compliances.head: Workplace safety
compliances.authority: Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation
compliances.brief: When a worker is injured or dies at the workplace, the employer tells the Ministry. All establishments also report injuries and occupational diseases through the Ministry's approved channels.
compliances.why: It employs staff.
compliances.appliesInWords: Employers (establishments registered with MoHRE).

due.text: Within 48 hours of the incident

compliances.dueText: The employer must inform MoHRE within 48 hours from the incident.
compliances.evidence: In case of an injury or death at the workplace, the employer must inform MoHRE within 48 hours from the incident.
compliances.note: The page names Ministerial Resolution No. 657 of 2022 as the basis. It states no penalty.

compliances.name: Renew work permits
compliances.head: Work permits
compliances.authority: Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation
compliances.brief: A work permit for a worker recruited from abroad, transferred, sponsored by family, or holding a Golden visa is valid for two years. It is renewed for the worker to go on working legally.
compliances.why: It employs staff and is registered with MoHRE.
compliances.appliesInWords: Establishments registered with MoHRE that employ workers on work permits.

due.text: Before each work permit expires (permits are valid for two years)

compliances.dueText: The permit is valid for two years. Renewal requires settling any outstanding fines for late issuance or non-renewal of the permit.
compliances.evidence: The permit is valid for two years. ... Settle any outstanding fines for late issuance or non-renewal of the permit.
compliances.note: The page gives the validity and says fines exist for non-renewal, but not the renewal window or the fine amounts. MoHRE's own service pages could not be opened (HTTP 503).

compliances.name: Health insurance for employees (Dubai)
compliances.head: Insurance
compliances.brief: An employer in Dubai enrols its employees in health insurance, pays the full cost, keeps the cover valid for the whole time they work for it, and shows the policy when a residence permit is issued or renewed. The minimum cover is the Essential Benefits Plan.
compliances.why: It employs staff in Dubai.
compliances.appliesInWords: Employers in the Emirate of Dubai.

due.text: From the day an employee starts, and at each issue or renewal of a residence permit

compliances.dueText: Ensure that employees' health insurance is valid throughout their service period, and produce a health insurance policy when issuing or renewing the residence permits of employees.
compliances.penalty: A fine of not less than AED 500 and not more than AED 150,000, doubled if the violation is repeated within one year, up to AED 500,000. The amounts for each violation are set by a resolution of the Executive Council.
compliances.evidence: An Employer must: enrol his employees in Health Insurance ... bear the cost ... ensure that his employees' Health Insurance is valid throughout their service period ... produce a Health Insurance Policy when issuing or renewing the residence permits of his employees.
compliances.note: The schedule of fines for each violation (an Executive Council resolution) was not read.

compliances.name: Register a new Emirati employee for pension
compliances.head: Payroll
compliances.authority: General Pension and Social Security Authority
compliances.brief: When a UAE national joins, the employer registers them with the pension authority through its employer portal and starts paying contributions.
compliances.why: You employ UAE nationals outside the Emirate of Abu Dhabi.
compliances.appliesInWords: Private-sector employers of UAE nationals in every emirate except Abu Dhabi (the Authority's page: 'employers in the private sector in all emirates of the country, except for the Emirate of Abu Dhabi').

due.text: Within 30 days of the employee joining

compliances.dueText: The employer must register the employee with the Authority within 30 days from the date of their joining service. (The Authority's service page says within one month; the shorter period is shown.)
compliances.penalty: The Authority's FAQ lists a fine of AED 5,000 for each insured person not registered, and an additional amount of AED 200 a day for each insured person for missing the registration deadline; it does not say how the two relate.
compliances.evidence: The employer must register the employee with the GPSSA within (30) days from the date of their joining service. (FAQ, https://gpssa.gov.ae/pages/en/help/faq, read 2026-11-12.) Service page: The service request must be submitted by the employer within one month of the new employee joining the establishment.
compliances.note: The Authority covers private-sector employers in every emirate except Abu Dhabi, whose employers deal with the Abu Dhabi Pension Fund (shown as its own item).

compliances.name: Tell the pension authority when an Emirati employee leaves
compliances.head: Payroll
compliances.authority: General Pension and Social Security Authority
compliances.brief: When an insured UAE national's service ends, the employer reports it to the pension authority.
compliances.why: You employ UAE nationals outside the Emirate of Abu Dhabi.
compliances.appliesInWords: Private-sector employers of UAE nationals in every emirate except Abu Dhabi.

due.text: Within one month of the end of service

compliances.dueText: Within a maximum of one month from the date of termination of their service.
compliances.penalty: An additional amount of AED 200 for each day of delay, for each insured person.
compliances.evidence: within a maximum of one month from the date of termination of their service

compliances.name: Pension for UAE nationals (Abu Dhabi Pension Fund)
compliances.form: Registration and monthly contributions with the Abu Dhabi fund
compliances.head: Payroll
compliances.brief: Private-sector employers in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi are outside the federal pension authority's scheme. They register their Emirati employees and pay pension contributions with the Abu Dhabi fund.
compliances.why: You employ UAE nationals in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi.
compliances.appliesInWords: Private-sector employers of UAE nationals in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi.

due.text: When you employ a UAE national: confirm the time limits with the Abu Dhabi Pension Fund

compliances.dueText: The Abu Dhabi fund's time limit for registering an employee and its date for paying contributions could not be read (its site returned an error on 2026-11-12). Confirm both with the Abu Dhabi Pension Fund before you rely on any date.
compliances.evidence: The employee must work for employers in the federal government and employers in the local government sector, except for the Emirate of Abu Dhabi and the Emirate of Sharjah, and employers in the private sector in all emirates of the country, except for the Emirate of Abu Dhabi
compliances.note: The General Pension and Social Security Authority's page says its scheme covers private-sector employers in all emirates except Abu Dhabi. The Abu Dhabi Pension Fund's own pages (pension.gov.ae) returned HTTP 503 and a system error on 2026-11-12, so its rules are not stated here.

compliances.name: Renew the establishment card
compliances.head: Establishment card
compliances.authority: Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs and Port Security
compliances.brief: The establishment card is the business's immigration file. It is renewed after it expires, and only if the trade licence is valid and fines on the establishment are paid.
compliances.why: It holds an establishment card.
compliances.appliesInWords: Private sector and free zone companies (and government bodies) that hold an establishment card.

due.text: Within 30 days of the card's expiry date

compliances.dueText: Renew within 30 days from the expiry date of the establishment card.
compliances.penalty: AED 100 for each month of delay, up to a maximum of AED 1,000.
compliances.evidence: A delay in renewing the establishment card for more than 30 days from its expiry date: AED 100 for each month of delay, up to a maximum of AED 1,000.
compliances.note: The page lists an annual renewal fee (AED 100 a year) but does not state how long a card is valid. In Dubai the card is renewed with the General Directorate of Residency and Foreigners Affairs.

compliances.name: Renew your Emirates ID
compliances.head: Emirates ID
compliances.authority: Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs and Port Security
compliances.brief: The Emirates ID can be renewed after it expires or as early as six months before. A late fee applies once a month has passed since expiry.
compliances.why: You hold an Emirates ID.
compliances.appliesInWords: UAE citizens, GCC citizens living in the UAE and residents.

due.text: Within one month after the card expires

compliances.dueText: The card can be renewed after its expiry or as early as six months before its expiry; a late fee is charged after one month since expiry.
compliances.penalty: AED 20 for each day of delay, up to a maximum of AED 1,000.
compliances.evidence: after one month since expiry ... a late fee of AED 20 per day will be charged, up to a maximum of AED 1,000.

compliances.name: Renew your residence visa
compliances.head: Residence visa
compliances.authority: Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs and Port Security
compliances.brief: A residence visa is renewed by the sponsor before it expires. Staying on after the visa and its grace period have run out is charged by the day.
compliances.why: You live in the UAE on a residence visa.
compliances.appliesInWords: Foreign residents and their sponsors.

due.text: Before the residence visa expires

compliances.dueText: Your sponsor must renew your residence visa before it expires.
compliances.penalty: AED 50 for each day of overstay.
compliances.evidence: Your sponsor must renew your residence visa before it expires.
compliances.note: The page says residents get grace periods of up to 6 months after a permit expires or is cancelled, depending on the resident's category.

compliances.name: Appoint an anti-money-laundering compliance officer
compliances.head: Anti-money laundering
compliances.brief: A designated non-financial business or profession appoints a qualified compliance officer at management level to run its anti-money-laundering programme. The supervisory authority must approve the appointment in writing beforehand, and be told of later changes to the role.
compliances.why: It is a designated non-financial business or profession.
compliances.appliesInWords: Designated non-financial businesses and professions supervised by the Ministry of Economy and Tourism.

due.text: When you start the activity (no date is stated)

compliances.dueText: No date is stated. The appointment must receive the prior written approval of the relevant Supervisory Authority.
compliances.penalty: AED 50,000 to AED 200,000 for failing to appoint a compliance officer with appropriate competence and expertise.
compliances.evidence: DNFBPs are required to appoint a qualified Compliance Officer ... The appointment must receive the prior written approval of the relevant Supervisory Authority.

compliances.name: Report suspicious transactions
compliances.form: Suspicious Transaction Report or Suspicious Activity Report (goAML)
compliances.head: Anti-money laundering
compliances.brief: When there are reasonable grounds to suspect that funds are linked to a crime, the business reports it to the Financial Intelligence Unit through goAML. There is no minimum amount, and attempted transactions count. Records are kept for at least five years.
compliances.why: It is a designated non-financial business or profession.
compliances.appliesInWords: Designated non-financial businesses and professions.

due.text: Without delay, once there is suspicion or reasonable grounds to suspect

compliances.dueText: Report to the FIU without delay when there are suspicions, or reasonable grounds to suspect, that the proceeds are related to a crime.
compliances.penalty: AED 100,000 to AED 500,000 for failing to promptly submit suspicious transaction reports to the Financial Intelligence Unit. The guidelines add that failing to report without delay is a federal crime.
compliances.evidence: DNFBPs are obliged to report STRs/SARs to the FIU without delay. ... There is no minimum reporting threshold; all suspicious transactions, including attempted transactions, should be reported regardless of the amount.

compliances.name: Register for sanctions list notifications
compliances.head: Anti-money laundering
compliances.authority: Executive Office for Control and Non-Proliferation
compliances.brief: Reporting entities register on the Executive Office's website to receive automatic updates to the UN and UAE sanctions lists, and screen their customers against those lists continuously.
compliances.why: It is a designated non-financial business or profession.
compliances.appliesInWords: Financial institutions, designated non-financial businesses and professions, and virtual asset service providers.

due.text: When you start the activity (no date is stated)

compliances.dueText: No date is stated. Reporting Entities are required to register with the Notification Alert System on the Executive Office's website.
compliances.penalty: AED 50,000 to AED 1,000,000 for failing to register on the Executive Office's website to receive sanctions notifications.
compliances.evidence: Reporting Entities are required to register [with the Notification Alert System]; they must "continuously screen their customers" against the Sanctions Lists.

compliances.name: Freeze and report a sanctions match
compliances.form: Confirmed Name Match Report or Partial Name Match Report (goAML)
compliances.head: Anti-money laundering
compliances.authority: Executive Office for Control and Non-Proliferation
compliances.brief: If a customer or party matches a name on the UN or UAE sanctions lists, the business freezes the funds without telling the person, and reports what it did through goAML.
compliances.why: It is a designated non-financial business or profession.
compliances.appliesInWords: Financial institutions, designated non-financial businesses and professions, and virtual asset service providers.

due.text: Freeze within 24 hours; report within five business days

compliances.dueText: Freeze without delay (immediately or in any case within 24 hours), and report through goAML within five business days from taking any freezing measure.
compliances.penalty: Imprisonment of one to seven years and/or a fine of AED 50,000 to AED 5,000,000 for breaching Cabinet Decision No. 74 of 2020. Administrative fines under Cabinet Resolution No. 71 of 2024: AED 500,000 to AED 1,000,000 for not freezing promptly; AED 50,000 to AED 100,000 for not promptly reporting the freeze.
compliances.evidence: immediately or in any case within 24 hours ... within five business days from taking any freezing measure
compliances.note: The Executive Office's page now names the reports CNMR and PNMR; its 2021 guidance called the first one a Funds Freeze Report (FFR).

compliances.name: Report large precious metals and stones transactions
compliances.form: Dealers in Precious Metals & Stones Report (DPMSR, goAML)
compliances.head: Anti-money laundering
compliances.brief: A dealer files a report for each cash transaction of AED 55,000 or more with an individual (resident or not), and each transaction of AED 55,000 or more with a company, in cash or by wire transfer. Linked transactions are added together. It is due even when nothing looks suspicious.
compliances.why: It is a dealer in precious metals or stones.
compliances.appliesInWords: Dealers in precious metals and stones.

due.text: For each transaction at or above AED 55,000

compliances.dueText: File a DPMSR for each transaction that meets the threshold. The guidance refers to 'predefined parameters and timelines' but states no number of days.
compliances.evidence: DPMS are required to file a Dealers in Precious Metals & Stones Report (DPMSR) ... When conducting a transaction with resident individuals for cash equal to or more than AED 55,000 or its equivalent in foreign currency.
compliances.note: The trigger and who must file were read. The time limit for filing was not: the Financial Intelligence Unit's report guides (uaefiu.gov.ae) returned HTTP 403, and the Ministry's Circular 08/AML/2021 states none.

compliances.name: Report cash and virtual-asset property deals
compliances.head: Anti-money laundering
compliances.brief: A broker or agent files a report for each purchase or sale of freehold property where cash of AED 55,000 or more is paid, in one payment or several, or where a virtual asset pays for any part of the price or the funds were converted from or to a virtual asset. It is due even when nothing looks suspicious.
compliances.why: It is a real estate broker or agent.
compliances.appliesInWords: Real estate brokers and agents.

due.text: For each freehold sale that meets the conditions

compliances.dueText: File a REAR for each transaction that meets the conditions. The guidance refers to 'predefined parameters and timelines' but states no number of days.
compliances.evidence: All real estate brokers and agents is required to file a REAR for: Purchase or Sale of freehold property / real estate where the method of payment includes cash and the amount is AED 55,000 or more; be it in a single payment or multiple payments.
compliances.note: The trigger and who must file were read. The time limit for filing was not: the Financial Intelligence Unit's report guides (uaefiu.gov.ae) returned HTTP 403, and the Ministry's Circular 05/2022 states none.

compliances.name: Hold the yearly general assembly (LLC)
compliances.head: Company meetings
compliances.brief: The manager of a limited liability company calls a general assembly of the partners at least once a year. It considers the accounts and the auditor's report and appoints the auditor: an LLC must have its accounts audited every year, and keep its accounting registers at its head office for at least five years.
compliances.why: It is a mainland limited liability company.
compliances.appliesInWords: Limited liability companies under the Commercial Companies Law.
compliances.dueText: At least once per year, within the four months following the end of the fiscal year of the company.
compliances.evidence: The general assembly shall be convened by an invitation from the manager or the board of managers at least once per year within the four months following the end of the fiscal year of the Company.
compliances.note: Read in the English text of Federal Decree-Law No. 32 of 2021 hosted by the Ministry. A 2025 amending decree-law exists and was not checked against this article.

compliances.name: Hold the annual general assembly (joint stock company)
compliances.head: Company meetings
compliances.authority: Ministry of Economy and Tourism (private JSC) or Securities and Commodities Authority (public JSC)
compliances.brief: The board of a joint stock company calls the shareholders' general assembly at least once a year. For private joint stock companies the Ministry ties the renewal of the company's registration to the filed assembly minutes and audited financial statements.
compliances.why: It is a joint stock company.
compliances.appliesInWords: Public and private joint stock companies.
compliances.dueText: At least once every year, within four months following the end of the fiscal year.
compliances.penalty: The Ministry's notice of 8 June 2026 to private joint stock companies: cautions, then fines of up to AED 10 million, with stricter measures for repeat offenders.
compliances.evidence: The general assembly of the shareholders shall be convened at the invitation of the board of directors at least once every year, within four months following the end of the fiscal year
compliances.note: For financial years ended 31 December 2025 the Ministry's notice asked private joint stock companies to hold the assembly no later than 30 June 2026.

compliances.name: File annual accounts (DIFC, company that is not small)
compliances.head: Accounts
compliances.brief: A DIFC private company that is not a small private company files audited accounts with the Registrar every year.
compliances.why: It is a DIFC company that is not small.
compliances.appliesInWords: DIFC private companies other than small private companies.
compliances.dueText: Audited accounts, within seven (7) months from the end of the financial year, where the company is a non-small private company.
compliances.evidence: Annual Accounts: Audited Accounts, within seven (7) months from the end of the financial year, where the company is a non-small private company.
compliances.note: From the compliance calendar of the DIFC handbook for private companies; the handbook says DIFC legislation prevails if the two differ. Public companies were not checked.

compliances.name: File annual accounts (DIFC, small private company)
compliances.head: Accounts
compliances.brief: A small DIFC private company files its accounts with the Registrar every year.
compliances.why: It is a small DIFC private company.
compliances.appliesInWords: DIFC small private companies (20 or fewer shareholders, or annual turnover of USD 5 million or less).
compliances.dueText: Accounts, within nine (9) months from the end of the financial year, for all other private companies.
compliances.evidence: Accounts, within nine (9) months from the end of the financial year, for all other private companies. ... A small private company is a company with less than or equal to 20 shareholders or an annual turnover of less than or equal to USD 5 million.
compliances.note: From the compliance calendar of the DIFC handbook for private companies; the handbook says DIFC legislation prevails if the two differ.

compliances.name: Report company changes to the DIFC Registrar
compliances.head: Registers
compliances.brief: A DIFC company files each change with the Registrar: directors, company secretary, registered address, name, activities, shareholders, share capital, articles, ultimate beneficial owners, auditor, financial year end, and special resolutions.
compliances.why: It is a DIFC company.
compliances.appliesInWords: DIFC private companies.

due.text: Within 30 days of the change

compliances.dueText: Within 30 days of any change (within 30 days of the appointment or cessation for an auditor; within 30 days of the date of the resolution for a special resolution).
compliances.evidence: Change of Director (s): Within 30 days of any change ... Change of Registered Address: Within 30 days of any change ... Change of Ultimate Beneficial Owners (s): Within 30 days of any change

compliances.name: Set up the beneficial ownership register (DIFC)
compliances.head: Registers
compliances.brief: A DIFC registered person keeps a register of its ultimate beneficial owners, records changes, and notifies the Registrar of each change. A company with nominee directors also keeps a register of them.
compliances.why: It is a DIFC company.
compliances.appliesInWords: DIFC registered persons.

due.text: Within 30 days of incorporation or registration

compliances.dueText: Establish a Beneficial Ownership Register within thirty (30) days of incorporation or registration; record changes within thirty (30) days of becoming aware of them; notify the Registrar within thirty (30) days of making the change.
compliances.penalty: A fine under Article 61(4) of the regulations' parent law; the amount was not read.
compliances.evidence: Each Registered Person which comes into existence on or after the Commencement Date shall establish a Beneficial Ownership Register within thirty (30) days of its incorporation or registration.

compliances.name: Pay final dues to a leaving employee (DIFC)
compliances.head: Payroll
compliances.brief: When employment ends, a DIFC employer pays the employee all remuneration and other amounts owed.
compliances.why: It is a DIFC employer.
compliances.appliesInWords: Employers in the DIFC.

due.text: Within 14 days after the termination date

compliances.dueText: Within fourteen (14) days after the Termination Date.
compliances.evidence: An Employer shall pay to an Employee, within fourteen (14) days after the Termination Date: (a) all Remuneration
compliances.note: The law provides a penalty for late payment that was not read.

compliances.name: Notify the DIFC data protection commissioner
compliances.head: Data protection
compliances.brief: A newly licensed DIFC entity that processes, or intends to process, personal data submits a notification through the DIFC portal. Hiring employees or serving customers counts as processing personal data.
compliances.why: It is a DIFC entity that handles personal data.
compliances.appliesInWords: DIFC entities that process personal data.

due.text: Within 6 months of the incorporation date

compliances.dueText: The completed notification must be submitted within six (6) months from the date of issuance of the DIFC license.
compliances.evidence: The completed notification must be submitted within six (6) months from the date of issuance of the DIFC license.
compliances.note: Registration fees by category: USD 1,250 (DFSA-regulated), USD 750 (non-regulated, except retail), USD 250 (retail). Fines were not read. Two DIFC documents state the start differently: the handbook's compliance calendar says within 6 months from the incorporation date, the data protection page says within six months from the date of issuance of the DIFC licence. The earlier one (incorporation) is shown.

compliances.name: Renew the DIFC data protection notification
compliances.head: Data protection
compliances.brief: The notification to the Commissioner is updated every year, and changes to the processing are notified. An entity that has appointed a data protection officer also submits a yearly assessment through the DIFC portal.
compliances.why: It is a DIFC entity that handles personal data.
compliances.appliesInWords: DIFC controllers that process personal data.

due.text: Every year (the DIFC portal sets the date)

compliances.dueText: The notification to the Commissioner of Data Protection must be updated annually.
compliances.evidence: The notification to the Commissioner of Data Protection must be updated annually.
compliances.note: Annual renewal fees: USD 500, USD 250 or USD 100 by category. The page does not give the day; DIFC handbooks indicate it is done with the licence renewal, which was not confirmed. Fines were not read.

compliances.name: Report a personal data breach (DIFC)
compliances.head: Data protection
compliances.brief: A DIFC controller tells the Commissioner about a personal data breach, and tells the people affected when the breach is likely to be a high risk to them.
compliances.why: It is a DIFC entity that handles personal data.
compliances.appliesInWords: DIFC controllers.

due.text: As soon as practicable after the breach

compliances.dueText: As soon as practicable in the circumstances.
compliances.evidence: as soon as practicable in the circumstances
compliances.note: The DIFC law sets no fixed number of hours.

compliances.name: File annual accounts (ADGM)
compliances.head: Accounts
compliances.brief: An ADGM company or LLP files its annual accounts with the Registrar. A small company (turnover up to USD 13.5 million and no more than 35 employees) may file an unaudited balance sheet instead of full audited accounts.
compliances.why: It is registered in ADGM.
compliances.appliesInWords: ADGM private companies and LLPs; public companies have six months.
compliances.dueText: The annual accounts must be filed within nine (9) months of the accounting reference date. For public companies, the period for filing is six (6) months, rather than nine.
compliances.evidence: the annual accounts must be filed within nine (9) months of its ARD. ... For public companies, the period for filing is six (6) months, rather than nine.
compliances.note: The date shown is for a private company. First accounts covering more than 12 months are due nine months from the first anniversary of incorporation. Restricted scope companies file only if the Registrar gives notice. The page states no late-filing penalty.

compliances.name: End-of-service gratuity and final pay (ADGM)
compliances.head: Payroll
compliances.brief: ADGM has its own employment rules in place of the federal labour law. An employee who completes one year or more of continuous employment is owed a gratuity when the employment ends, whatever the reason: 21 days' basic wage for each of the first five years of service and 30 days' basic wage for each further year. UAE and GCC nationals enrolled in the pension scheme, and employees who chose a pension or savings scheme instead, are not owed it.
compliances.why: It is an ADGM employer.
compliances.appliesInWords: ADGM establishments that employ staff.

due.text: Within 21 calendar days of the employee's termination date

compliances.dueText: The gratuity is owed at the termination of employment. All wages and any other amounts owed to the employee (other than variable pay such as bonuses or commissions) must be paid within 21 calendar days of the employee's termination date.
compliances.evidence: An Employee who completes continuous employment of 1 year or more is entitled to a gratuity payment at the termination of the Employee's employment, regardless of the reason for termination. ... After the termination of employment, an Employee is entitled to all wages and any other amounts owed to the Employee (excluding any variable payments such as bonuses or commissions) within 21 calendar days of the Employee's termination date. ... ADGM is a financial free zone generally exempt from most of the UAE federal civil and commercial laws, including the UAE Federal Labour Law.
compliances.note: Read in the Employment Affairs Office's guidance on the ADGM Employment Regulations 2024 (published 18 February 2025), sections 22 and 24. The regulations themselves were not opened. No penalty was read.

compliances.name: Renew the ADGM data protection registration
compliances.head: Data protection
compliances.brief: ADGM entities that process personal data register as data controllers and renew every year for USD 300. A change in the registered particulars is notified as it happens, free of charge.
compliances.why: It is an ADGM entity that handles personal data.
compliances.appliesInWords: ADGM registered entities that process personal data.
compliances.dueText: Data protection registrations must be renewed annually; the renewal fee must be paid within the one-month grace period following the anniversary of incorporation.
compliances.penalty: A fixed monetary penalty of USD 450 on the data protection fees page; ADGM's annual filings page says late payment could result in a fine of USD 750. The two official pages differ.
compliances.evidence: Data protection registrations must be renewed annually. ... within the one-month grace period following the anniversary of incorporation
compliances.note: The date shown is the end of the grace month and assumes the licence date you gave is the date of incorporation.

compliances.name: Report a change of beneficial owner (ADGM)
compliances.form: Notification of change in beneficial ownership
compliances.head: Registers
compliances.brief: ADGM entities keep a record of the required particulars of their beneficial owners and report changes to the Registrar. Branches of foreign companies and partnerships are outside these rules.
compliances.why: It is registered in ADGM.
compliances.appliesInWords: All legal entities in ADGM except branches of foreign companies or foreign partnerships.

due.text: Within 15 days of the change

compliances.dueText: Report changes to the Registrar within 15 days of a change.
compliances.penalty: Up to a Level 9 fine (USD 54,000,000 is the maximum the page states).
compliances.evidence: must keep a record of the required particulars of their beneficial owners ... report changes to the Registrar within 15 days of a change

compliances.name: Report a personal data breach (ADGM)
compliances.head: Data protection
compliances.brief: An ADGM data controller reports a personal data breach to the Office of Data Protection through the Online Registry Solution.
compliances.why: It is an ADGM entity that handles personal data.
compliances.appliesInWords: ADGM data controllers.

due.text: Within 72 hours of becoming aware of the breach, where feasible

compliances.dueText: Without undue delay and, where feasible, not later than 72 hours after becoming aware of the breach.
compliances.evidence: without undue delay and, where feasible, not later than 72 hours after becoming aware of them

compliances.name: Notify the appointment or resignation of a data protection officer (ADGM)
compliances.head: Data protection
compliances.brief: An ADGM entity that appoints a data protection officer, or whose officer resigns, tells the Commissioner of Data Protection.
compliances.why: It is an ADGM entity that handles personal data.
compliances.appliesInWords: ADGM data controllers and processors that have a data protection officer.

due.text: Within one month of the appointment or resignation

compliances.dueText: Notify the Commissioner of Data Protection within one month of appointing a DPO or of the DPO's resignation.
compliances.evidence: must notify the Commissioner of Data Protection within one month
compliances.note: Which entities must appoint an officer was not read.

compliances.name: Submit audited financial statements (DMCC)
compliances.form: Audited Financial Statements and Summary Sheet
compliances.head: Accounts
compliances.brief: Every DMCC company, including subsidiaries and branches, uploads its audited financial statements and the auditor's signed summary sheet on the DMCC member portal each year. The auditor must be on DMCC's Approved Auditors List.
compliances.why: It is a DMCC company.
compliances.appliesInWords: All DMCC companies including subsidiaries and branch companies.
compliances.dueText: Within six months after the end of each financial year.
compliances.evidence: A DMCC member company must upload the auditor's signed and stamped Audited Financial Statements Summary Sheet and the Audited Financial Statements ... within six months after the end of each financial year.
compliances.note: The guideline states no penalty. An older DMCC sheet said 90 days; this guideline is dated 29 April 2025. A foreign company's DMCC branch is entity type 'branch' in the checker and is not reached by this condition.

compliances.name: Submit the yearly audit report (JAFZA)
compliances.head: Accounts
compliances.brief: A JAFZA FZE or FZCO gives the Authority an updated audit report every year, through the Dubai Trade portal. The auditor must hold a Dubai economic department licence and be appointed by a company resolution.
compliances.why: It is a JAFZA company.
compliances.appliesInWords: FZE and FZCO establishments in the Jebel Ali Free Zone.

due.text: Every year (no date is stated)

compliances.dueText: FZE and FZCO establishments must provide an updated audit report to the Authority annually. The page states no date.
compliances.evidence: FZE and FZCO establishments must provide an updated audit report to the Authority annually.
compliances.note: No deadline and no penalty are on the page. The financial year must be between 6 and 18 months.

compliances.name: Quarterly safety performance report (Abu Dhabi)
compliances.head: Workplace safety
compliances.authority: Your Abu Dhabi sector regulatory authority
compliances.brief: An entity with an approved occupational safety and health management system reports its safety performance (incidents, lost days and similar) to its sector regulator every quarter, starting the quarter after the system is approved.
compliances.why: It has an approved safety management system in Abu Dhabi.
compliances.appliesInWords: Entities in Abu Dhabi with an approved OSH management system under ADOSH-SF.
compliances.dueText: Q1: 1st to (maximum) 15th of April; Q2: 15th of July; Q3: 15th of October; Q4: 15th of January of the following year.
compliances.evidence: Entities with an approved OSHMS shall submit Quarterly OSH performance reports ... Q1 1st to (Maximum) 15th of April; Q2 ... 15th of July; Q3 ... 15th of October; Q4 ... 15th of January (Following Year)
compliances.note: The same mechanism requires a yearly report of the monetary cost of OSH incidents within the first quarter of the next year, and an annual third-party audit report within 30 calendar days of the audit.

compliances.name: Notify a serious workplace incident (Abu Dhabi)
compliances.head: Workplace safety
compliances.authority: Your Abu Dhabi sector regulatory authority
compliances.brief: An entity notifies its sector regulator of a fatality or other serious incident at the workplace (serious injury, serious occupational illness, serious dangerous occurrence), then sends the investigation report.
compliances.why: It has an approved safety management system in Abu Dhabi.
compliances.appliesInWords: Entities in Abu Dhabi covered by ADOSH-SF (mandatory for entities with an approved OSH management system and medium risk entities).

due.text: Within 24 hours for a fatality; within 3 working days for other serious incidents

compliances.dueText: Within 24 hours of an incident which results in a fatality; within a maximum of 3 working days for other serious incidents. The investigation report follows within 30 calendar days.
compliances.evidence: The entity shall officially notify the concerned SRA as follows: (i) Within 24 hours of an incident occurring at a workplace which results in Fatality; (ii) Within maximum of 3 working days from the date of an incident

compliances.name: Renew the Dubai Customs business code
compliances.head: Registers
compliances.brief: The Dubai Customs business code is valid only as long as the trade licence. After the licence is renewed, the business renews its customs registration (fee AED 25) to go on clearing goods.
compliances.why: It imports or exports goods through Dubai.
compliances.appliesInWords: Businesses registered with Dubai Customs.

due.text: After each trade licence renewal, within 60 days of the licence expiry date

compliances.dueText: The validity of the business code is associated with the validity of the licence; renewal can be requested only after the licence is renewed. Customs policy: renew on expiry or within the grace period of sixty (60) days from the licence expiry date.
compliances.penalty: The customs client code is suspended if not renewed within sixty (60) days from the date of its expiry.
compliances.evidence: The validity of this Business code is associated with the validity of the License. Clients can request for the renewal of the business code only after the renewal of the License from the competent licensing authority.
compliances.note: The 60-day grace period and the suspension come from a Dubai Customs policy in force from 22 October 2009, published in its Customs Policies booklet; no later text was found. Only Dubai was read; Abu Dhabi's TAMM pages could not be opened.

confirmations.dueText: Licence renewal and confirmation statement: on the expiry date of the licence and no later than 30 days after licence expiry.
confirmations.evidence: License Renewal and Confirmation Statement: On the expiry date of license and no later than (30) days after license expiry (compliance calendar, DIFC handbook DIFC-CS-GL-12 Rev.06, approved 29 September 2026).

confirmations.dueText: JAFZA only: the trade licence can be renewed within three months before the expiry.
confirmations.evidence: Trade License can be renewed within three months before the expiry. ... AED 1,000 fine for delay in renewing an expired license. (JAFZA 'Renew License' guide, dated 26 April 2024.) Other free zones were not read.
confirmations.penalty: JAFZA: AED 1,000 fine for delay in renewing an expired licence.

confirmations.dueText: Core benefits for each monthly period must be paid to a qualifying scheme by the twenty first (21st) day of the next calendar month.
confirmations.evidence: an Employer shall be in contravention of Article 66(7) if Core Benefits in respect of any monthly period are not paid by the Employer by the twenty first (21st) day of the next calendar month to a Qualifying Scheme (DIFC Employment Law, Consolidated Version No. 5, July 2025). Existing item is verified true but says the day was not found.
confirmations.penalty: A fine as set out in Schedule 2 of the law; the amount was not read.

confirmations.dueText: Employers must pay all outstanding wages, other entitlements and gratuity within 14 days of the termination of the contract.
confirmations.evidence: Employers must pay all outstanding wages, other entitlements and gratuity within 14 days of the termination of the contract. (u.ae, updated 15 Oct 2026; also Article 53 of Federal Decree-Law No. 33 of 2021.) Existing item is verified true but gives no number of days.

confirmations.dueText: Annual accounts (private company or LLP): within nine (9) months of the accounting reference date; public companies six (6) months.
confirmations.evidence: the annual accounts must be filed within nine (9) months of its ARD. ... For public companies, the period for filing is six (6) months, rather than nine. Fills the gap in the existing item's note; also given as the new item ae_x_adgm_accounts.

confirmations.dueText: Contributions are due from the first day of the month after the month they relate to and may be extended until the 15th day of that month.
confirmations.evidence: GPSSA FAQ: contributions 'may be extended until the 15th day of that month'; late payment bears 'an additional amount calculated at 0.1%' for each day of delay. Existing item is verified true with no penalty stated.
confirmations.penalty: An additional amount of 0.1% of the overdue contributions for each day of delay.

confirmations.dueText: Not confirmed: the time limit for new joiners is still not on any page that could be opened.
confirmations.evidence: u.ae (updated 08 Dec 2025): 'A worker who does not subscribe to the Unemployment Insurance Scheme will be fined 400 AED. A worker who does not pay the premiums will be fined 400 AED.' iloe.ae policy terms: the certificate is cancelled if a payment is missed for more than 90 days from its due date. The four-month limit appears only in mohre.gov.ae search snippets (site returned HTTP 503).
confirmations.penalty: AED 400 for not subscribing; AED 400 for not paying premiums (u.ae).
